Not French food
Sep 2026 • Couples
September 24, 2026

The restaurant is located on the second floor of the Sofitel Hotel. It was Friday night, yet the restaurant was surprisingly empty. Unfortunately, the food explained why I left feeling so disappointed. We ordered the onion soup, mussels, and duck.

The onion soup was a major disappointment. It came with croutons mixed in, but there was no cheese, and the soup was overly sweet and lacked depth and flavor. The preparation was so unusual that it barely resembled the French onion soup I know. For a restaurant presenting itself as a French dining establishment, this was particularly disappointing.

The mussels were even worse. I expected them to be served in a flavorful, buttery, wine-based sauce, but there was almost no sauce at all. Instead, they appeared to have simply been steamed with onions and were completely lacking in flavor. To make matters worse, the mussels were tough and did not taste fresh. This was not what I would expect from a French restaurant, especially one receiving such positive reviews.

The duck was only average. It was not terrible, but it was certainly nothing memorable. I also found the dish unnecessarily dry and would have expected a proper sauce to accompany the meat. In my view, sauces are an important element of French cuisine, and the lack of sauce throughout the meal was particularly disappointing.

Overall, I honestly do not understand how this restaurant has received such high reviews. The food was poorly executed, lacked flavor, and, in my experience, did not represent French cuisine well at all. I came expecting a proper French dining experience and left extremely disappointed.

The one positive was the service. The staff were attentive and courteous throughout the meal.

I was also surprised to see that the bill included a service gratuity as well as additional fees that were not clearly explained to us. I would have appreciated greater transparency about these charges before paying the bill.

Based on this experience, I would not return. The quality of the food did not come close to what I expected from a French restaurant in a Sofitel Hotel, and the high ratings set expectations that the meal siimply did not meet. Andrew

Le 17 French bistro is a must try
Mar 2026 • Couples
Le 17 French bistro at Sofitel Saigon Plaza was a great night out.
We enjoyed lovely attentive service from Johnny and his team.
Steak tartare and French onion soup were tasty and well presented appetisers.
Lobster, rib eye (perfectly medium rare) and mussels were equally as impressive, as were the sides and brûlée and apple tartine for deserts.
Great selections of wines at reasonable prices rounded out a good menu offering.
Highly recommend.
